text: Why don't we drink pig milk? Pigs are mammals. They nurse their young, and farms are full of them. So the milk is there. The problem is getting it out. A cow stores milk in a big chamber inside her udder, called a cistern. When she's milked it flows for several minutes. A sow has no cistern at all. Her milk sits deep in the tissue, and she only releases it when her piglets ask. They nose and massage her belly for about a minute. Then a hormone called oxytocin kicks in, and the milk flows for just ten to twenty seconds. After that she's done for the next hour. A cow also has four large teats. A sow has twelve to fourteen small ones, each giving a tiny amount. And a sow won't stand still for a milking machine. So pig milk is perfectly drinkable. It's just the hardest milk on the farm to collect.
